title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §4 of the 'Longue Marche' notes, titled 'Sections d'extensions et anneaux de valuation généraux' (sections of extensions and general valuation rings). The words 'd'extensions' are a later insertion. The page itself only fixes notation for what follows.

(1) For a connected scheme X, E_X = π1(X) denotes the profinite fundamental group, regarded as an outer group. That is, it is defined only up to inner automorphism, with no base point chosen.

(2) If X̃ is a profinite universal covering of X, then E_X^{X̃} = π1(X; X̃) = Aut_X(X̃) is the 'precise' fundamental group, an honest profinite group. Here X̃ is the projective limit of a cofinal system of connected finite étale covers.

For X = Spec(A), with A a ring and most often a field, he writes E_A and E_A^{Ã}. Here Ã is an A-algebra such that Spec(Ã) is a universal cover. For a field K this is the absolute Galois group Gal(K^sep/K) with a chosen separable closure.

(3) For a geometric point ξ, E_X^ξ = π1(X, ξ) = E_X^{X̃(ξ)}, where X̃(ξ) is the universal cover pointed at ξ.

The next page continues the setup:
- A geometric point amounts to a point x together with an algebraically closed extension Ω of k(x), not necessarily an algebraic closure.
- E_X^Ω ≅ E_X^{\overline{k(x)}}.
- Functoriality E(f): E_X → E_Y holds as outer homomorphisms.

The purpose is to set up the language of base-point-free ('outer') versus pointed fundamental groups. This is needed to discuss sections of the extension 1 → π1(X_{\bar K}) → π1(X) → Gal(\bar K/K) → 1. The heading indicates these sections will be studied via general (non-discrete, arbitrary rank) valuation rings, presumably attaching to a section a valuation or 'point' on a model.
errors: The phrase about uniqueness of the universal cover is hard to read. A universal profinite cover is determined only up to non-unique isomorphism: its automorphism group is π1 itself. The precise group E_X^{X̃} therefore depends on X̃ up to inner automorphism, which is exactly why E_X is an outer group. If the text claims uniqueness up to unique isomorphism, that would be inaccurate, but the reading is uncertain.
No mathematical errors otherwise; the page is purely notational.

ideas.what: Fundamental group as an outer group (base-point-free) versus the precise group Aut_X(X̃) attached to a chosen profinite universal cover
ideas.modern_name: outer fundamental group / pro-universal cover, fundamental groupoid viewpoint
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V; also Esquisse d'un programme and the letter to Faltings (1983) use the outer-group viewpoint

ideas.what: Notation E_K^{\bar K} for absolute Galois groups, with geometric points given by arbitrary algebraically closed extensions
ideas.modern_name: absolute Galois group with base point

ideas.what: Programmatic heading linking sections of fundamental group extensions to general valuation rings
ideas.modern_name: valuation-theoretic approach to the (birational) section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Koenigsmann (2005), Pop (birational section conjecture, 2010s), Esnault–Wittenberg and others
ideas.where_published: Section conjecture stated in the letter to Faltings (1983); a valuation-theoretic treatment by Grothendieck is not known to me in published form

missed.claim: The section title shows Grothendieck, in the Longue Marche period (c. 1981), planning to relate sections of Galois/fundamental-group extensions to general (non-discrete) valuation rings. This prefigures the valuation-theoretic local theory of sections later developed by Koenigsmann and Pop. This page contains only notation, so the substance, if any, is on the following pages.
missed.quote: 4. Sections d'extensions et anneaux de valuation généraux.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would document that the valuation approach to the section conjecture, credited to Koenigsmann/Pop, was envisaged by Grothendieck. Whether the following pages contain actual results needs checking.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a notational preamble on outer versus precise fundamental groups, which is routine. Only the section heading hints at an early link between sections and general valuations, which may be of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'revêtement universel profini de $\mathcal{E}_X$ [?]' should read 'revêtement universel profini de $X$'.

In (3) the notation is $\mathcal{E}_X^{\xi}$ with $\xi$ a geometric point; on the next page, 'Le choix de $\mathcal{G}$' should be 'Le choix de $\xi$', and '$\mathcal{E}_X^{\mathcal{G}}$' should be '$\mathcal{E}_X^{\xi}$'.
'd'extensions,' is a later insertion above the title, placed between 'Sections' and 'et anneaux'. The '52' is a section/page marker; the '104' in the corner is the archive page number.
The phrase after '(ce qui le détermine' is uncertain; it plausibly concerns uniqueness up to (non-unique) isomorphism.
